caption: What if humans could photosynthesise? Chlorophyll in your skin would soak up red and blue light and bounce back green, turning you green. Recipe: sunlight + water + carbon dioxide makes sugar, with oxygen as the leftover. Most of India gets 4 to 7 kWh of sunshine per square metre every day. Your skin covers about 2 square metres, but only about half faces the Sun at once. And even the best plants can turn at most about 4.6% of sunlight into food. So a whole sunny day standing still would give you roughly 200 kcal, less than one samosa. You need around 2,000 kcal a day, which would take about 10 square metres of sunlit green skin, roughly a 10x10 ft room. Plot twist: one animal comes close. The sea slug Elysia chlorotica keeps the chloroplasts from the algae it eats, turns emerald green, and can go nine months or more without eating. Would YOU trade lunch for sunshine? 👇
